warnings: CORRECTED 2026-08-24 — full pixel re-survey of this sheet. Grid pinned first from the drawing itself: x 1=981, 2=1305, 3=1681, 4=2004 px (107.7 px/m across all three bays) and y A=720, B=932, C=1303, D=1674, E=1886 px (106.0 px/m across all four bands), both consistent to under 1%. Beams were then found by per-bay/per-band coverage sweeps, distinguishing a beam (a face PAIR at coverage 1.0) from a bare grid line (a single line at 0.75-0.83). Five dummy grid lines were added to the master, every one of them read off a printed dimension: y A'=-1.00 and B'=4.30, x 1'=1.00, 2'=4.40, 2''=5.90.

Two beams were on the wrong row and are now re-assigned: (1) the grid3-4 beam recorded as A3-A4 actually sits on A' (-1.00) — the grid3-4 bay has no beam at row A at all; (2) the grid1-2 beam recorded as C1-C2 actually sits on B' (4.30) — the grid1-2 bay has no beam at row C. Both are the same failure mode: a beam that frames a projection/offset line got snapped to the nearest named row.

Five beams were missing entirely and have been added: the two B3' verticals of the north projection (A'3-A3 and A'4-A4, span 1.00 each), and three B1 verticals in the A-B band standing on the new dummy columns 1'(1.00), 2'(4.40) and 2''(5.90) — each traced y=732..924 px, i.e. the full row A to row B span of 2.00. The three dummy columns come straight off the top margin, which prints 1.00 from grid 1, 1.40 from grid 2, and 0.60 before grid 3; the beams' measured centres (1.09, 4.27, 5.96) sit within half a beam width of those printed face dimensions.

Element count went 27 -> 32 beams. The horizontal runs at rows A and B were NOT split at the new dummy columns: the printed marks change only at the named grids (B2 for grid1-2, B3 for grid2-3), so each keeps its full marked length, following the same convention Makham set for house 41's B4 = 4.10.
Printed but NOT promoted to grid lines, because a sweep finds no beam on them: 1.60 above row A (left margin) and 0.50 below row A. Recorded in the grid master's unassigned_dimensions.

This plan is denser and more heavily photocopied than most sheets in the set. The 4 perimeter/main-grid beam runs (rows A-D, columns 1-4) were read with reasonable confidence (0.6-0.7 per element). Two small entrance-canopy slabs (S0, +0.10, cantilevered past row A near grid1 and grid3) print short offset dimensions (1.40m / 0.60m) that could not be confirmed as marking a real column+beam terminus versus a pure slab edge at this scan resolution — treated as slab-only edges (no dummy grid added, beams B2/B3 recorded as single continuous A1-A2 / A2-A3 segments) per the 'no dummy grid for a slab-only edge' rule. See the grid master's warnings for the same note.

A short stub beam marked 'B1'' appears near grid C1 (inside a small storage room, ~row B-C at column 1) with a small square symbol next to it; its far endpoint was not legible with enough confidence to assign a grid_ref, and per the schema a beam element must never be recorded with a prose description in place of grid_ref_start/grid_ref_end — so this stub was left OUT rather than mis-recorded. Its rebar spec is still present in specs.B1' via หน้า31 (identical to B1) in case a future higher-resolution pass locates it.

The D3-E3 / D4-E4 corner of the plan carries a 1-step (10cm) floor drop matching the architectural 'DROP 1 STEP' note for the รับแขก/เฉลียง area (สถ. หน้า03) — beams there are printed at level (+0.30) instead of the (+0.40) used everywhere else, and two short 'B1'(+0.30)' stub beams mark the step edge itself; those two short stubs were not independently positioned (folded into the adjacent D3-E3/D4-E4 main segments already recorded) since their exact sub-metre placement could not be confirmed.

S0 (2 occurrences, small entrance canopy slabs, +0.10) and S1 (2 occurrences, small enclosed slab bays with an X-hatch pattern, +0.40) carry no printed grid mark of their own — grid_refs below are the nearest bounding grid points, approximate per the same convention already used for stair/undefined-symbol markers in this dataset (e.g. house 28's GS marker).
